alignments.note: Preposition plus relative rendered by the single word 'when' (rule 30), headed on the preposition, which carries the temporal sense.
Verb with its auxiliary; the subject is the explicit noun phrase, which the ASV fronts, so the unit stands apart from it under rule 25.
Construct noun with the supplied 'the'; the rectum carries a suffix and no article morpheme (rule 29).
Rectum with the relational 'of' (rule 19); discontinuous around the possessive.
The lə of lēʾmōr has no English realization (rule 27).
Interrogative particle takes the fronted question auxiliary 'Wilt' (rule 17).
Verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17); discontinuous around the negative.
Dative preposition rendered as a bare English indirect object, leaving it no word (rule 40).

The verbless 'what are these to thee' is recast as 'what thou meanest by these'; the preposition of the predicate carries the supplied relational verb together with the 'by' written for it (rule 49). Head on 'by', the English preposition written for this morpheme, as rule 49 heads 'which belonged to the house' on 'to' and rule 24 asks for the token most directly realizing the source lexeme; heading on 'meanest' would put a preposition's unit on a supplied verb. The competing reading of the unit's edges marks the preposition unrepresented and 'meanest' added, but dropping the verb removes the preposition's own relation and nothing else.
Suffix takes the subject pronoun of the recast clause (rules 18, 40).

review_notes: Corrected the target head of the lāk unit from 'meanest' (t020) to 'by' (t021). The unit's edges were right — rule 49's relational-verb clause puts the supplied verb with the preposition — but rule 49 heads such a unit on the English preposition written for it, as in 'which belonged to the house' headed on 'to', and rule 24 asks for the token most directly realizing the source morpheme's lexeme.
'thou meanest by' remains the reading taken for the recast predicate lāk; the competing reading (unrepresented preposition, added 'meanest') is named in that unit's note.

Everything else in the verse is unchanged: kaʾăšer fuses to 'when' under rule 30, the interrogative particle takes the fronted 'Wilt' under rule 17, and both lə morphemes left wordless by the ASV's recasting are unrepresented under rules 27 and 40.
